message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide for pulling “detailed” interface data on the most common platforms (Linux/Unix, macOS, Windows, and via SNMP). Feel free to pick the section that matches your environment; each snippet can be run directly from a terminal or adapted into a script. --- ## 1️⃣ Linux / Unix | Tool | What it shows | Typical command | |------|---------------|-----------------| | **`ip`** | Interface state, MAC, MTU, IPs, flags | `ip link show eth0` | | **`ethtool`** | Driver, firmware, speed, duplex, autoneg, stats | `ethtool -i eth0`
`ethtool -S eth0` | | **`lshw`** | Full hardware tree (PCI bus, driver, firmware) | `sudo lshw -class network -short` | | **`nmcli`** | NetworkManager status & config | `nmcli device show eth0` | | **`ss` / `netstat`** | Socket usage per interface | `ss -i` | | **`sysfs`** | Low‑level sysfs attributes | `cat /sys/class/net/eth0/address` | ### Example – Pull all details for `eth0` ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash IF=eth0 echo "=== ip link ===" ip link show $IF echo "\n=== ethtool -i ===" ethtool -i $IF echo "\n=== ethtool -S ===" ethtool -S $IF echo "\n=== lshw ===" sudo lshw -class network -short | grep "$IF" echo "\n=== nmcli ===" nmcli device show $IF ``` --- ## 2️⃣ macOS | Tool | Command | |------|---------| | **`ifconfig`** | Interface flags, IP, MAC, MTU | `ifconfig en0` | | **`networksetup`** | DNS, proxy, VPN settings | `networksetup -getinfo Ethernet` | | **`system_profiler SPNetworkDataType`** | Full hardware + driver | `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType | grep -A10 "Ethernet"` | | **`scutil --dns`** | DNS resolution tables | `scutil --dns` | --- ## 3️⃣ Windows | PowerShell Cmdlet | What it shows | Example | |-------------------|---------------|---------| | `Get-NetAdapter` | Adapter status, MAC, speed, driver | `Get-NetAdapter -Name "Ethernet" | Format-List *` | | `Get-NetIPConfiguration` | IP config, DHCP, DNS | `Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet"` | | `Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapter` | WMI view of adapter | `Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapter | Where-Object {$_.NetConnectionID -eq "Ethernet"} | Format-List *` | | `Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty` | Advanced settings | `Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name "Ethernet"` | --- ## 4️⃣ SNMP (for remote devices) | OID | Meaning | How to query | |-----|---------|--------------| | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.1` (`ifIndex`) | Interface index | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public host.ifIndex` | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2` (`ifDescr`) | Description | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public host.ifDescr` | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5` (`ifSpeed`) | Speed (bits/sec) | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public host.ifSpeed` | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.8` (`ifOperStatus`) | Operational status | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public host.ifOperStatus` | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10` (`ifInOctets`) | Bytes received | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public host.ifInOctets` | | `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.16` (`ifOutOctets`) | Bytes transmitted | `snmpwalk -v2c -c public host.ifOutOctets` | **Example (Linux CLI)** ```bash snmpwalk -v2c -c public 192.168.1.1 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.2 # list all interface names snmpget -v2c -c public 192.168.1.1 1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.5.1 # speed of ifIndex 1 ``` --- ## 5️⃣ Programmatic Retrieval (Python example) ```python import subprocess import json def run(cmd): return subprocess.check_output(cmd, shell=True, text=True) # Linux example if_name = "eth0" details = { "link": run(f"ip -j link show {if_name}"), "driver": run(f"ethtool -i {if_name}"), "stats": run(f"ethtool -S {if_name}") } print(json.dumps(details, indent=2)) ``` --- ## Quick Checklist | Item | Why you might need it | Tool | |------|-----------------------|------| | MAC address | Physical identification | `ip link` / `ifconfig` | | IP configuration | Connectivity | `ip addr` / `Get-NetIPConfiguration` | | Link speed & duplex | Performance tuning | `ethtool -i` / `Get-NetAdapter` | | Driver & firmware | Compatibility & bugs | `lshw` / `Get-WmiObject` | | Statistics (bytes, errors, drops) | Troubleshooting | `ethtool -S` / SNMP `ifInOctets` | | Autonegotiation status | Auto‑configuration | `ethtool -a` | | VLAN tags | Layer‑2 segmentation | `bridge vlan show` / `Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty` | --- ### TL;DR * **Linux** → `ip`, `ethtool`, `lshw`, `nmcli` * **macOS** → `ifconfig`, `system_profiler` * **Windows** → PowerShell `Get-NetAdapter`, `Get-NetIPConfiguration` * **Remote** → SNMP OIDs (`ifDescr`, `ifSpeed`, `ifOperStatus`, etc.) Pick the set that matches your platform, run the command(s), and you’ll have a full dump of everything the OS knows about that interface.
